web.security.title: Security and data handling
web.security.intro: This page states the launch requirements Brief enforces and identifies controls that must be externally approved before real publisher content is enabled.
web.security.eu.title: EU hosting
web.security.eu.body: The MVP requires application infrastructure, Postgres, and private object storage in EU regions. Production release evidence must verify backups, point-in-time recovery, private networking, transport encryption, and object-storage encryption before launch.
web.security.ai.title: AI confidentiality
web.security.ai.body: Local development uses the exact registered GLM-5-Turbo contract through Z.AI's official Coding Plan endpoint. No production AI provider is selected: production fails closed until account-specific confidentiality, training-use, retention, deletion, region and transfer, security, and subprocessor evidence is accepted. AI answers can be incomplete and must cite the sources they use.
web.security.subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
web.security.subprocessors.body: No production subprocessor set is accepted yet. Local development may call Z.AI for model inference and Tinyfish Search for optional web discovery; neither development capability authorizes real publisher content. The production list is generated only from accepted deployment decisions and must disclose every enabled service.
web.security.access.title: Human access
web.security.access.body: Publishers cannot see client chats. Platform staff normally see operational metadata only. Restricted content access requires an MFA-authenticated, time-limited, exact-scope grant with a reason and customer approval or a recorded exception; every access is append-only logged and reviewed.
web.security.retention.title: Retention, deletion, and exports
web.security.retention.body: Deleted chats disappear immediately and are purged from active storage within 30 days unless a legal hold applies. Company-account content has a 180-day recovery window. Runtime events are retained for 24 hours, deleted memories remain reversible for 30 days, and authenticated users can request the exports defined for their role.
web.security.encryption.title: Encryption and incident contact
web.security.encryption.body: Transport encryption is mandatory. Production may not launch with publisher documents until database and object-storage encryption at rest are verified. Security, privacy, and incident requests use the contact below.
web.privacy.title: Privacy policy summary
web.privacy.intro: This launch summary must remain consistent with the executed privacy notice, data-processing agreement, provider contracts, and configured retention controls.
web.privacy.data.title: Data we process
web.privacy.data.body: Brief processes account and company identity, publisher issue files and extracted text, delivered archive metadata, client chats and saved memories, notification settings, billing and AI usage records, security events, and support authorization logs. Restricted content is not used for routine staff analytics.
web.privacy.purpose.title: Why we process it
web.privacy.purpose.body: Processing is limited to authenticated distribution, durable client archives, search, cited AI answers, user-requested web research, notifications, billing and limits, exports, security, customer support, deletion, and required legal retention.
web.privacy.retention.title: Retention and deletion
web.privacy.retention.body: Deleted chat content leaves active storage within 30 days unless legal hold applies; company accounts have a 180-day recovery period; backups use a 30-day rolling window; billing records are retained for 10 years; security logs for 12 months; restricted support and authorization audit logs for 24 months; operational content-free logs for 30 days.
web.privacy.rights.title: Access, export, correction, and deletion
web.privacy.rights.body: Authenticated users can access and export the records defined for their role, correct account settings, delete eligible chats and memories, and request company deletion through support. Published delivered issues remain part of the client company’s durable archive; legal, accounting, security, recovery, and legal-hold duties can delay deletion.
web.privacy.providers.title: Providers and international processing
web.privacy.providers.body: No production provider or international-processing posture is accepted yet. Local development may send model requests to Z.AI and, when explicitly enabled, search queries to Tinyfish; these development capabilities are not approved for real publisher content. The launch notice must name every exact enabled provider, region, retention, training-use, deletion, subprocessor, and transfer posture accepted through the production decision process.
web.references.title: Official provider references
web.legal.publisher.title: Publisher terms summary
web.legal.publisher.intro: This product summary is not a substitute for the executed publisher agreement and jurisdiction-specific legal review.
web.legal.publisher.content.title: Publisher content and permissions
web.legal.publisher.content.body: The publisher controls its uploaded issue documents and client access, confirms it may distribute that content, and remains responsible for its commercial relationships with clients.
web.legal.publisher.delivery.title: Durable delivery
web.legal.publisher.delivery.body: Published issues are immutable. Issues already delivered remain in each client company’s archive; corrections are delivered as a new issue. Only a restricted support action may hide published material for security, legal, or compliance reasons.
web.legal.publisher.commercial.title: Commercial boundary
web.legal.publisher.commercial.body: Brief does not process or track publisher-client subscription payments. The platform separately sells prepaid AI usage to client companies and exposes publishers only to aggregate context-pull metrics for their own documents.
web.legal.client.title: Client terms summary
web.legal.client.intro: This product summary is not a substitute for the executed client agreement and jurisdiction-specific legal review.
web.legal.client.ai.title: AI limitations
web.legal.client.ai.body: Users know they are interacting with AI. Answers may be incomplete or wrong, must cite the sources they use, and do not replace professional judgment. Web research is explicit and policy controlled.
web.legal.client.billing.title: AI plans and credits
web.legal.client.billing.body: Client companies prepay monthly and additional AI credits through the platform. Monthly credits are consumed first and expire at period end; additional credits expire after 12 months. Only client-company admins manage billing and limits.
web.legal.client.rights.title: Access, export, and deletion
web.legal.client.rights.body: Authenticated users may read delivered issues and export visible content while access remains valid. Private and shared-chat creators may delete their chats; company deletion is a support-request flow subject to recovery, accounting, security, and legal-hold retention.
web.legal.processing.title: Data processing and security summary
web.legal.processing.intro: The executed data-processing agreement controls. This page summarizes the canonical product boundary and must be updated with final provider contracts and regions before launch.
web.legal.processing.roles.title: Data roles and purpose
web.legal.processing.roles.body: Publishers control uploaded publications and delivery access; client companies control employee access and chats; Brief processes content and metadata only to provide distribution, archive search, cited AI, billing, support, security, and required retention.
web.legal.processing.providers.title: Providers and transfers
web.legal.processing.providers.body: The approved launch contracts must name every exact enabled authentication, billing, email, hosting, AI, and web-search service, including region, retention, training use, deletion, security, subprocessor, and transfer terms. Real content remains blocked until all applicable provider evidence is accepted.
web.legal.processing.support.title: Restricted support access
web.legal.processing.support.body: Restricted support access is exceptional, exact-scope, time-limited, MFA protected, reasoned, tamper-resistant logged, and periodically reviewed. Customer approval is linked unless a security, legal, or compliance exception records why it was skipped.
web.legal.contactMissing: The security and privacy contact is not configured. Production activation remains blocked until a monitored address is verified.
